name: CO-06
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district with an 11-point partisan lean
Incumbent Jason Crow running with a $3.2 million war chest and $2.7 million on hand
Republican challenger Jason Clark shows no reported fundraising
Prediction markets price Crow at roughly 96% to win
model.rationale: The fundamentals point firmly to Crow: an 11-point Democratic lean, a favorable environment, incumbency, and a large financial edge over a challenger with no visible fundraising. Prediction markets agree at about 96% for Crow, so the forecast stays in Safe D territory with only a modest trim from the fundamentals-only view.
model.watch: Any late surge of outside spending against Crow or a wave-level national environment shifting several points toward Republicans would be the main thing to watch.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Jason Crow, the Democratic incumbent in Colorado's 6th District, seeks another term in a seat whose partisan lean favors his party by about 11 points. He enters the general election with a substantial financial advantage, having raised roughly $3.2 million and holding about $2.7 million on hand. Republican nominee Jason Clark reports no fundraising on file, and minor-party and independent candidates in the field show negligible resources.

No public general-election polling is available for this race, and no expert raters have issued ratings, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, money, and markets. Prediction markets price Crow's chances at about 96 percent. The combination of a favorable district, a well-funded incumbent, and an underfunded challenger makes this a Safe Democratic race.
